findings.reason: Confirmed against published Lemma A.6 and Corollary A.7, pp. 258–260, arXiv v3 source, and items 104/119. For Z_2+2Z_2[sqrt(-2)], all unit norms are a^2+8b^2 (a odd), hence 1 modulo 8; odd scalar squares supply all of 1+8Z_2. For Z_2+4Z_2[i] the same argument uses a^2+16b^2. The primitive reduced forms of discriminants -16 and -32 give class numbers 1 and 2, respectively. The corrected nonmaximal dyadic cases are right, including the split etale case under 'unramified': with t=v_2(f), norm images are maximal for t=1 and d_E-valuation 0 or 2; 1+4Z_2 for t=2 and d_E-valuation 0; 1+8Z_2 otherwise. The wild INDEX depends on t and v_2(d_E), not merely whether 2 ramifies; this does not mean those data determine E_2 itself. Keep the abstract local-index genus formulas and record the faulty dyadic evaluation as a source error. Independent residue checks covered all eight quadratic etale square classes modulo 64; no claim is made to repeat the red team's 3000-discriminant scan.

Confirmed, with a corrected rescaling witness. Published pp. 235–237 and item 87 omit k_0 from the local-density argument. Take Q=x^2+3y^2, f=1, k_0=2, k_1=1, k_2=3, and the canonical representative l=2 modulo 3. The left side includes (1,1), whereas rho_Q(2;3)=0; a sufficiently large disc meets the remaining size hypotheses (e.g. theta_l=3/4, eta=1/10, delta=4). CRT requires rho_Q(k_0 k_1 l;k_1 k_2). The Proposition 9.25 proof separately needs (R/k_0)^theta_l <= (A/k_0^2)^(1-3eta). Use A=10^12, R=10^7, k_0=10^5, theta_l=3/4, eta=1/10: both printed curvature assumptions hold, but 10^(3/2)>10^(7/5) violates the rescaled one. Unlike the proposed witness, k_0 is integral and theta_l is admissible. This establishes a proof gap, not a counterexample to the conclusion of 9.25. For the application of 9.26, k^2<=A^eta gives the repaired curvature inequality; p. 245 already has the correct rho_Q(m;(D_0D_1)^2). Retain the separate E25 rescaling repair.

Confirmed against published pp. 218–219, v3 Lemma 112 and item 74. For n>=1 and a in A_p intersect K_p, the index is (p+1)p^(2n-1), by counting two oppositely directed length-n paths from the common midpoint. For a translating the midpoint a positive distance it is p^(2n). Exact GL_2 congruence counts for p=2,3,5 and n=1,2 independently check the centered case. Correct the proposed fix at n=0: the two subgroups coincide, so the ratio is 1 for every a. Thus use p^(2n) when n=0 or a is not in K_p, and (1+1/p)p^(2n) otherwise. The bound between p^(2n) and (3/2)p^(2n) suffices for the application; the upper bound on the denominator measure used on p. 219 still has the needed direction.

Confirmed against published pp. 162/172, v3 and item 8, but the 'nothing downstream' assessment of compactness is too strong. Multiplication by rational -1 makes every idele class have positive infinite component; a rational multiplier between two positive representatives must be positive. This proves the claimed positive quotient is the entire double-coset target, not an index-two subgroup. Valuation parity maps both the full and positive-infinite idele square-class groups onto the infinite discrete direct sum over finite primes, proving noncompactness in both quaternion signatures. Use locally compact abelian groups and a bijective double-coset norm map. Also repair p. 254/footnote 11 and item 123, which explicitly rely on the same false compact-fibre assertion. A replacement is available from the volume definition in section 7.2: conjugation by xi_1 preserves Haar measure on G(A)^+ (the semisimple adjoint determinant has absolute value one locally), so the simply connected Hecke volume equals m_{G(A)^+}(Omega intersect c Omega c^-1)^-1, c=ctr(xi). It factors through c directly; no compactness of the fibre is needed. Record compactness as a proof error at that use, not merely an innocuous misprint.

Confirmed with the disjunctive qualification. The published conclusion, pp. 253–256, and item 124 require overlap of (2-1/theta_l)/3 and 1/(2+2/(1-theta)); at theta_l=2/3 and theta=1/2 both equal 1/6, with no room for the positive margins. Huxley's endpoint gives 18/131<1/6, so choose theta_l strictly between 131/208 and 2/3; alternatively a theta<1/2 allows a sufficiently close theta_l>2/3. Huxley is not indispensable if the Ramanujan improvement is supplied, but the current brief supplies neither gap-closing choice and omits the small-norm/entropy assembly. Extend it using items 123/124 and the exact overlap inequality. Distinguish alternative exponent inputs from simultaneous prerequisites; do not claim that either strict improvement suffices with arbitrarily poor value of the other exponent.

Confirmed as a reuse and ownership defect, with a narrower library comparison. I read the three cited declarations at Tau Ceti f790474 and the reviewed Multiquadratic audit (layers 2–3 built). Preserve HE.0's local-different items 36 and 37 as well as 10–15 and 114: the proposed 'keep only' list accidentally drops them. HE.0's current dependency contract does not name Multiquadratic.

Restrict the sufficient criterion to Xi_1 (both primes), and the item-123 correlation estimate to the p_1 condition actually proved. Equations (56)–(57), pp. 254–255, put the epsilon loss on the stronger-decay side; use 1-theta-epsilon and take epsilon small relative to the existing epsilon_1 margin.
